title: Section Landing
prompt:
Create a SECTION LANDING page for the yearbook, in the exact same visual system as the source spread. Desktop, 1280px.

The page is a full-bleed deep navy section divider with almost no page furniture.

- A small tracked uppercase monospace line at the top left: SECTION 02
- A large section title in the display serif at 72px, near-white cream, left aligned, breaking to at most 14 characters per line: CSE - CLASS OF 2026
- A single gold hairline rule under the title, no longer than 120px
- One short paragraph in the body sans, cream at 70 percent opacity, at most 3 lines, at most 55 characters per line: The whole batch, in the order they signed. Six names to a page, and the last page is still full.
- A small tracked uppercase monospace line at the bottom left: 148 MEMBERS / 62 SIGNED
- A small tracked uppercase monospace folio at the top right in gold: 02
- At the bottom, a row of small tracked uppercase monospace navigation links separated by generous space: COVER / SECTIONS / INDEX / YOUR PAGE

Do not add a photograph, an illustration, a mascot, an emblem, a texture, a pattern, a gradient background, a hand-drawn element, an emoji or a button. The section landing is typographic only. Gold appears on exactly one thing: the folio in the top right. Use ONLY the fonts, colors, spacing and component styles defined in the design system. Do not introduce any fonts, colors, or visual styles not in the design system.

title: Your Own Yearbook Page
prompt:
Create a PERSONAL YEARBOOK PAGE - the page a student opens to find their own entry. Same visual system as the source spread. Desktop, 1280px, cream paper stock, two columns.

LEFT COLUMN:
- A running head row at the top: small tracked uppercase monospace YOUR PAGE on the left, a small folio 48 on the right, with a 1px hairline rule beneath
- A large white T-shirt illustration on a cream mat in a 3:4 plate, filling about 60 percent of the column width, covered in many visible marker marks in the marker colours - at least eight different marks scattered across the fabric: a handwritten scrawl, a heart, a star, a smiley, a flower doodle, a small note, a set of initials, a crossed-out scribble. Every mark is drawn ON the white fabric, inside the shirt outline, never on the mat
- Beneath the shirt, a name in the display serif at 32px: AARAV SHARMA
- Beneath the name, one line of body sans: B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering, 2026

RIGHT COLUMN:
- A heading in tracked uppercase monospace at 12px: SIGNED BY
- A 1px hairline rule above the directory
- A two-column directory of the people who signed it. Twelve rows, each a single line: a small tracked uppercase monospace name on the left, and on the right a small sample of that person's actual handwriting in the handwriting font, short and casual - things like legend, bestie, dk, ship it, yay, tysm. Use these twelve names: MEGHNA NAIR, ARJUN MENON, MAYANK IYER, DIYA PRASAD, ROHAN BHATT, ISHAAN RAO, SANA QURESHI, VIVAAN JOSHI, ANANYA DESAI, KABIR SETHI, TARA MENON, NEEL PATEL
- At the foot of the right column, a single line of body sans at 15px, at most 2 lines: Twenty-four marks, seventeen friends, one month that went too fast.

Do not add photographs, faces, avatars, illustrations of people, emoji, stickers outside the shirt, tape, washi, paper texture, doodles in the margins, or buttons. The display serif appears exactly once, on the name AARAV SHARMA. The handwriting samples in the directory are the only handwriting outside the fabric. Use ONLY the fonts, colors, spacing and component styles defined in the design system. Do not introduce any fonts, colors, or visual styles not in the design system. Gold appears nowhere on this page.
